what_happened: Task 313's own completed plan and its shipped lint script header (lint-roadmap-batch-proposals.sh:74-79) already named this task's objective as the exact trigger for the lint's parse layer needing rescoping, and recorded it as an accepted follow-up cost -- settling the dispatch's 313-disposition question directly from existing artifacts with no ambiguity.

state-management-schema.md's Project Entry Fields table omits the 'priority' field even though it is modelled in state-schema.json and known to validate-state.sh (3 references) -- a reader consulting only the human-facing reference would not learn the field exists.

This plan's harvested file_scope collides with two concurrently-dispatched siblings: agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/validate-state.sh (task 531's sole declared entry) and agent-system/extensions/core/index-entries.json (task 597). The live ROADMAP.md Run 1 rationale asserts 'None of the four collides with another run-1 member', which is measurably wrong once 603's plan declares validate-state.sh. No edge exists in either direction; an operator-side edge declaration is needed before either reaches implement.

Diffing the live ## Open work section against a fresh 'roadmap-integration.sh --print' render cost two commands and decisively collapsed a feared migration: 13 of 137 task lines differ, 12 are stale truncations the retention parser froze and 1 is an outdated title snapshot, with 0 annotations and 0 EXT-BLOCKED tokens live. The per-task description override is therefore pure drift machinery, so retiring it is a zero-loss net deletion that also repairs 13 lines -- a conclusion the research pass had left as an open migration obligation.

Three of the dispatch description's carried figures failed re-derivation: priority is populated on 15 of 142 records (1 critical, 4 high, 10 medium, 127 null), not 14 with 133 null (a figure also internally inconsistent at 14+133=147); the wave distribution is 83/33/13/5/2/1 over 137 open records, not the parenthetical 83/30/18/9/1/1; and '--prune reports retained=141' does not reproduce in either mode (retained is 0 under --prune, 137 under --regenerate). pruned=0 did reproduce.
git-commit-phase.sh dropped 'agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/lint/lint-agent-contracts.sh' from a phase commit pathspec: not contained in this task's declared file_scope.

migrate-roadmap-next-to-state.sh's paragraph-block splitter (blank-line-delimited) merged an entire GFM 'tight' bullet list -- the live specs/ROADMAP.md's own style, no blank line between consecutive bullets -- into one unsplit block, so no individual bullet could be attributed to its matching batch. The hand-written test fixture used blank-line-separated bullets and never exercised this, so the bug was invisible until the script ran against the real live file during Phase 7.

The same migration script's bullet-to-batch attribution heuristic (first integer token matching a batch's task_ids) was also applied to free-standing PROSE paragraphs (not bullets), causing a general policy paragraph that merely mentioned a batch's task id in passing (e.g. 'the claimant roster is five: 431, 459, 505, ...') to be mis-attributed into that batch's rationale instead of staying in next_postamble. Fixed by scoping attribution to blocks that are genuinely bullets (start with '- ').

The Agent tool's subagent_type roster does not recognize a brand-new agent .md file (roadmap-agent) created earlier in the same session -- no mid-session reload. Both live /roadmap demonstrations were performed via a general-purpose agent explicitly instructed to read and follow agents/roadmap-agent.md verbatim as its own contract (the documented Self-Execution Fallback path), rather than a literal roadmap-agent dispatch.

The full roadmap_batches/roadmap_notes inversion round-tripped cleanly end to end on the first live attempt once the two migration bugs were fixed: migrate-roadmap-next-to-state.sh's losslessness accounting gate passed with zero unaccounted lines against the real, hand-authored ## Next body (193 authored lines, 9 batches), and roadmap-integration.sh --regenerate produced a byte-identical second render immediately after, with no manual cleanup needed.
